title_en: Homily I on the Holy Pascha
author: Hesychius of Jerusalem
addressee: a congregation of faithful Christians gathered for the Paschal vigil
occasion: Delivered during the Paschal night vigil in Jerusalem to celebrate Christ's resurrection, proclaim his victory over death and the devil, and invite the faithful to share in the triumph through the veneration of the cross.
argument: The homily opens by depicting the Paschal night as brighter than the stars because the risen Christ has conquered the world and the invisible enemy, enabling believers to share in his victory through the cross. It contrasts the concealment of the Logos under the Law (the bushel) with his revelation on the cross (the lampstand), illuminating the whole world. Using typology, it parallels the Mosaic rod that drove off Egypt's plagues with a rod akin to the wood of the cross that ends human sins, and contrasts Pharaoh's drowning with the devil's defeat, and Adam's outstretched hands (bringing death) with Christ's outstretched hands (bringing salvation). The good thief's immediate entry into paradise models the faith that grants believers access to heaven. The resurrection is celebrated as a cosmic event—opening tombs, raising bones, splitting heavens, and inaugurating the King's ascent—where Christ, having sanctified humanity in the womb and vivified the dead in the tomb, ascends as victorious king, glorious commander, and unbeaten charioteer to present the redeemed to the Father.

outline.move: The preacher hails the Paschal night as radiant with Christ's victory, urges the faithful to cling to the saving cross, and declares the Logos now revealed on the lampstand of the cross after being hidden under the bushel of the Law.

Typological parallels exalt the cross: Rome honors it, Paul writes immortal epistles and enrolls himself as a slave of the cross, the Mosaic rod prefigures the cross's power over sin, Pharaoh's drowning prefigures the devil's defeat, and Adam's death-bringing gesture is reversed by Christ's saving outstretched hands; the good thief's instant paradise exemplifies the cross's power.

The congregation is invited to imitate the thief's faith, crying 'Remember me,' while the day itself proclaims the resurrection as a cosmic spectacle of opened tombs, rejoicing souls, and the heavenly King ascending in light.

Christ's two concealments (womb and tomb) are shown as sanctification and vivification; his resurrection raises Adam's race, opens paradise, plunders Hades, and culminates in his royal session at the Father's right hand, concluding with a doxology.

cast.name: Hesychius of Jerusalem
cast.who: Presbyter of Jerusalem, mid-5th century, delivering this Paschal homily.

cast.name: Jesus Christ
cast.who: The risen Lord, Logos incarnate, conqueror of death and the devil, celebrated as Sun of Righteousness and King.

cast.name: The Devil / Satan
cast.who: The invisible enemy defeated by the cross and taken captive by Christ.

cast.name: Hades
cast.who: The realm of the dead, plundered by the risen Christ.

cast.name: Adam
cast.who: The first man whose outstretched hands brought death and whose 'flock' is raised by the second Adam.

cast.name: Eve
cast.who: The first woman, comforted by the resurrection.

cast.name: Pharaoh
cast.who: Egyptian ruler drowned pursuing Israel, a type of the devil's defeat.

cast.name: Paul
cast.who: Apostle who boasted in the cross and wrote 'immortal' epistles.

cast.name: The Good Thief
cast.who: The penitent crucified with Jesus who asked to be remembered and entered paradise that day.

cast.name: The Father
cast.who: Receives the victorious Son and grants him session at his right hand.

cast.name: Israel
cast.who: The people delivered through the Red Sea, prefiguring the salvation of the faithful.

cast.name: Egyptians
cast.who: The forces of Pharaoh drowned in the sea, a type of the demonic host defeated by Christ.

cast.name: Jews
cast.who: Those for whom the cross was a stumbling-block, contrasted with the Gentiles who receive it as wisdom.

cast.name: Rome
cast.who: The imperial city depicted as honoring the cross in its public square.

cast.name: Jerusalem
cast.who: The city where the homily is delivered and where the cross is venerated.

voices.speaker: Hesychius (preacher)
voices.how_marked: First-person plural exhortations ('Παραμείνωμεν', 'Μιμησώμεθα', 'λέγοντες'), direct address to congregation ('ἀδελφοί', 'ἀγαπητέ'), and narrative description.

voices.speaker: Jesus Christ (quoted)
voices.how_marked: Introduced by φησίν / λέγει with Gospel sayings (John 16:33; Luke 23:43) and speaking to the Father (Heb 2:13 // Isa 8:18).

voices.speaker: The Good Thief (quoted)
voices.how_marked: Direct speech introduced by Τὶ γὰρ καὶ φησίν; and the words «Μνήσθητί μου, κύριε, ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ σου.»

voices.speaker: The Day personified (quoted)
voices.how_marked: Personified speech: «Ἐν τῷ ἐμῷ δρόμῳ εἶδον θέαμα καινόν...»

voices.speaker: The Father (quoted)
voices.how_marked: Speech introduced by 'Καὶ ἤκουσεν παρὰ τοῦ Πατρός' and quotation of Ps 109:1 LXX: «Κάθου ἐκ δεξιῶν μου...»

key_terms.sense: The Christian Passover/Easter feast celebrating Christ's passion and resurrection.
The cross of Christ as the instrument of victory, object of veneration, and cosmic sign of salvation.
Visible signs or representations of the cross (e.g., on standards, in public spaces) that proclaim Christ's triumph.
The pre-existent Word of God, incarnate in Jesus, hidden under the Law and revealed on the cross.
The Mosaic Law, figured as a 'bushel' that concealed the Light/Word from unbelievers.
The lampstand on which the lamp (the Word) is set; here, the cross as the exaltation of Christ for all to see.
Typological correspondence between Old Testament events (Moses' rod, Pharaoh, Adam) and Christ's cross/resurrection.
Christ's rising from the dead, which raises the whole human race (Adam's flock) and opens paradise.
The realm of the dead, plundered by the risen Christ.
The garden of God reopened by the cross; the good thief enters it immediately, and all the redeemed are destined for it.
Christ's definitive conquest of the world, the devil, and death, shared by believers.
The proclamation of the resurrection as 'good news of joy' on this day.

scripture: The author follows the Septuagint (LXX) for Old Testament citations and allusions. Psalm numbering follows the LXX (e.g., LXX Ps 23:7 = MT/English Ps 24:7; LXX Ps 109:1 = MT/English Ps 110:1). New Testament quotations are from the Greek text. In modern citations: use standard English book names (Genesis, Exodus, etc.) with LXX psalm numbers noted parenthetically when they differ from Hebrew numbering (e.g., 'Psalm 24:7 (LXX 23:7)').
uncertain: Exact year of delivery within Hesychius' episcopate (c. 412–451).
Whether the homily was preached at the Anastasis (Holy Sepulchre) or another Jerusalem church.
The precise identity of the 'immortal epistles' of Paul referenced (likely a rhetorical flourish for his canonical letters).
Whether the personified 'Day' speech is a quotation from a lost homily or the author's own composition.
The textual state of the 'rod' passage (ῥάβδος δὲ συγγενείᾳ πρὸς τὸ τοῦ σταυροῦ ξύλον) which is syntactically awkward and possibly corrupt.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Jerusalem — The city where the homily is delivered and where the cross is venerated.
_unresolved_facts.fix: Jerusalem appears only in the title, as Hesychius's see ("presbyter of Jerusalem"). The text never says where the homily was preached or that the cross was venerated there. Drop the claim or mark it as inferred.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Delivered during the Paschal night vigil in Jerusalem
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Τὴν ἱερὰν ταύτην νύκτα δᾳδουχίαις ἱεραῖς πανηγυρίσωμεν
_unresolved_facts.fix: The text supports a Paschal night celebration with sacred torchlight processions ("this holy night"). It does not name Jerusalem as the place. Say "on the Paschal night" and treat the Jerusalem setting as inferred from the title.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Egyptians — The forces of Pharaoh drowned in the sea, a type of the demonic host defeated by Christ.
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Μία ῥάβδος μωσαϊκὴ τὰς τῶν Αἰγυπτίων μάστιγας ἀπήλασεν
_unresolved_facts.fix: Only the Egyptians' plagues (μάστιγας) are mentioned, and the Mosaic rod drove them off. The text says Pharaoh, not the Egyptians, is drowned ("Φαραὼ καταποντοῦται"). Rewrite as "the Egyptians, whose plagues the Mosaic rod drove away".

_unresolved_facts.claim: Israel — The people delivered through the Red Sea, prefiguring the salvation of the faithful.
_unresolved_facts.fix: The source says only that Pharaoh is drowned while pursuing Israel. The Red Sea and the faithful's salvation are not stated here. Use "Israel, pursued by Pharaoh".

_unresolved_facts.claim: Paul — Apostle who boasted in the cross and wrote 'immortal' epistles.
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: οὐκ ἐπῃσχύνθη τὸν σταυρόν, τὸ σκάνδαλον τῶν Ἰουδαίων
_unresolved_facts.fix: The text says Paul "was not ashamed of the cross" and "enrolled himself as a slave of the cross". He is not said to boast. He writes "ἀθανάτους ἐπιστολάς" (immortal letters).

_unresolved_facts.claim: Jews — ... contrasted with the Gentiles who receive it as wisdom.
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: τὴν τῶν ἐθνῶν μωρίαν σοφίας ἐπεσπάσατο φυλακτήριον
_unresolved_facts.fix: Paul "drew the folly of the Gentiles to himself as a safeguard of wisdom" (a protective charm of wisdom). The Gentiles are not said to receive the cross as wisdom.

_unresolved_facts.claim: The Good Thief ... The penitent crucified with Jesus
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Μιμησώμεθα τοῦ ἀνδροφόνου τὴν ἀγαθὴν γνώμην, μᾶλλον δὲ τοῦ πνευματοφόρου
_unresolved_facts.fix: The preacher calls him "the murderer" (ἀνδροφόνου) and "robber" (λῃστήν), then corrects himself to "Spirit-bearer" (πνευματοφόρου) because of his later faith. The brief's source_forms omit λῃστήν. "Good thief" is a modern label. "Penitent" is not in the text, which praises his "good intent".

_unresolved_facts.source_quote: ὁ διάβολος διὰ τὸν σταυρωθέντα ἡττήθη
_unresolved_facts.fix: The source never uses "Satan". It uses διάβολος, τὸν ἀόρατον πολέμιον, τὸν τύραννον and στρατὸν διαβολικόν. Name the entry "The Devil".

_unresolved_facts.claim: Adam — ... whose 'flock' is raised by the second Adam.
_unresolved_facts.fix: "Second Adam" is not in the text. Say "the herd/flock (ἀγέλη) of Adam, raised together with Christ".

_unresolved_facts.claim: ascends as victorious king, glorious commander, and unbeaten charioteer
_unresolved_facts.fix: ἄλειπτος means "unanointed" or "unrubbed". It does not mean "unbeaten" (that would be ἀήττητος). Render it literally, e.g. "like an unanointed charioteer", with a note that the reading is odd or possibly corrupt.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Exact year of delivery within Hesychius' episcopate (c. 412–451).
_unresolved_facts.fix: The title calls him a presbyter, not a bishop. Write "within Hesychius' presbyteral career (c. 412–451)". This also matches the cast entry.
